title: The Escaping Mass Has No Integrable Majorant

meta.author: Lean Genius
originalContributions: escaping_no_integrable_majorant: the headline — the parent's escaping-mass sequence escaping n = 𝟙_[n,n+1) admits no integrable majorant. If g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞ dominates every bump pointwise (∀ n, escaping n ≤ g), then ∫⁻ g = ∞. This is the obstruction explaining why the Dominated Convergence Theorem cannot rescue the escaping mass that makes Fatou's inequality strict: DCT requires a single integrable majorant, and none exists. Proof: the bumps [n,n+1) tile [0,∞), so any common majorant is ≥ 1 there, and ∫⁻ g ≥ ∫⁻ 𝟙_[0,∞) = volume (Ici 0) = ∞ by lintegral_mono + lintegral_indicator_one + Real.volume_Ici.

one_le_of_majorizes_escaping: the key pointwise lemma — any majorant of all bumps is ≥ 1 on the whole ray [0,∞). For x ≥ 0 the bump indexed by n = ⌊x⌋₊ covers x (⌊x⌋₊ ≤ x < ⌊x⌋₊ + 1 via Nat.floor_le and Nat.lt_floor_add_one), so 1 = escaping ⌊x⌋₊ x ≤ g x.
prerequisites: MeasureTheory.lintegral_mono: monotonicity of the lower Lebesgue integral, f ≤ g ⟹ ∫⁻ f ≤ ∫⁻ g, used to bound ∫⁻ g below by the integral of the indicator of [0,∞)
MeasureTheory.lintegral_indicator_one: ∫⁻ x, s.indicator 1 x = μ s for measurable s, giving ∫⁻ 𝟙_[0,∞) = volume (Ici 0)
Real.volume_Ici: the Lebesgue measure of a closed ray [a,∞) is ∞
Nat.floor_le / Nat.lt_floor_add_one: the floor sandwich ⌊x⌋₊ ≤ x < ⌊x⌋₊ + 1 placing x ≥ 0 inside the bump [⌊x⌋₊, ⌊x⌋₊ + 1)

Monotonicity of the lower Lebesgue integral; applied to the domination 𝟙_[0,∞) ≤ g to push the infinite measure of the ray into ∫⁻ g.

overview.historicalContext: Fatou's lemma, the monotone convergence theorem, and the dominated convergence theorem (DCT) are the three pillars of Lebesgue integration, logically linked MCT ⇒ Fatou ⇒ DCT. The parent entry fatou-lemma-oq-01 exhibits the escaping-mass sequence 𝟙_[n,n+1) — a unit bump marching to +∞ — as a witness that Fatou's inequality ∫⁻ liminfₙ fₙ ≤ liminfₙ ∫⁻ fₙ can be strict (0 < 1): mass escapes to infinity and is lost in the pointwise liminf. The natural question is why the dominated convergence theorem — which forces equality and convergence of the integrals — does not apply to repair this. DCT carries exactly one extra hypothesis beyond pointwise convergence: a single integrable majorant g dominating every fₙ. This entry settles the obstruction side: the escaping sequence has NO such majorant, so DCT is simply inapplicable, and the strictness of Fatou's inequality is consistent with DCT. The positive companion — the explicit g ± fₙ Fatou ⇒ DCT derivation — is supplied by the follow-up child entry fatou-lemma-oq-01-oq-02-oq-01.
overview.problemStatement: Prove that the escaping-mass sequence escaping n = 𝟙_[n,n+1) of the parent Fatou entry has no integrable majorant: there is no g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞ with finite Lebesgue integral and escaping n ≤ g pointwise for all n. Equivalently, every pointwise majorant of all the bumps has ∫⁻ g = ∞.
overview.proofStrategy: Two steps. (1) one_le_of_majorizes_escaping: for x ≥ 0, the bump indexed by n = ⌊x⌋₊ contains x — the floor sandwich Nat.floor_le and Nat.lt_floor_add_one give ⌊x⌋₊ ≤ x < ⌊x⌋₊ + 1, i.e. x ∈ Ico ⌊x⌋₊ (⌊x⌋₊ + 1) — so escaping ⌊x⌋₊ x = 1, and the domination hypothesis gives 1 ≤ g x. (2) escaping_no_integrable_majorant: thus 𝟙_[0,∞) ≤ g pointwise (using zero_le off the ray), so by lintegral_mono, ∫⁻ g ≥ ∫⁻ 𝟙_[0,∞) = volume (Ici 0) = ∞ (lintegral_indicator_one on the measurable ray, then Real.volume_Ici); top_le_iff forces ∫⁻ g = ∞.
keyInsights: The bumps tile the ray. Because the half-open intervals [n, n+1) for n = 0, 1, 2, … partition [0, ∞), a function dominating every bump is forced to be ≥ 1 on the entire ray — a set of infinite Lebesgue measure — so its integral is infinite.

This pinpoints which DCT hypothesis fails. DCT differs from plain Fatou only by demanding an integrable majorant; the escaping sequence is excluded from DCT precisely by lacking one, which is exactly why the parent's Fatou inequality is allowed to be strict.
The obstruction is sharp and elementary: it needs nothing about the integrals ∫⁻ escaping n = 1 themselves, only the pointwise tiling of [0,∞) and the infinitude of its Lebesgue measure.

Paired with the child fatou-lemma-oq-01-oq-02-oq-01 (the positive g ± fₙ Fatou ⇒ DCT derivation), this closes the Fatou ↔ DCT narrative: an integrable majorant collapses the liminf/limsup bracket to equality, and its absence is what frees the escaping mass to violate it.

conclusion.summary: This entry proves the obstruction half of the Fatou ↔ DCT story for the parent's escaping-mass witness: the sequence escaping n = 𝟙_[n,n+1) has no integrable majorant. Any g dominating every bump is ≥ 1 on the ray [0,∞) (since the bumps tile it, via the floor sandwich), so ∫⁻ g ≥ volume (Ici 0) = ∞. This shows the Dominated Convergence Theorem cannot apply to the escaping mass, consistent with the parent's strict Fatou inequality. 72 lines, 2 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: Identifies exactly which DCT hypothesis the escaping-mass witness violates — the integrable majorant — completing the obstruction side of the bracketing narrative opened by the parent fatou-lemma-oq-01 and answered on the positive side by the child fatou-lemma-oq-01-oq-02-oq-01 (the explicit g ± fₙ Fatou ⇒ DCT derivation).
openQuestions: Quantify the escape: show ∫⁻ over [0,N) of any common majorant grows at least linearly in N, making the divergence rate explicit.
Characterize which marching-bump sequences (varying width or height) do admit an integrable majorant, drawing the exact boundary of DCT applicability.
